product_from_film: Liquid lets a user view a portfolio and request a trade suggestion through a chat interface, then confirm the order.
explains_well: The demo follows portfolio request, position request, analysis, suggestion and an explicit confirmation button.
unclear: The trade rationale and sizing details are dense and brief compared with the clear prompt and confirmation steps.
scenario: Ask to see a portfolio, request a long NVDA position, inspect an analysis/suggestion card and select Confirm buy.
product_clear_basis: The show me my portfolio prompt produces a portfolio card at 21s; the trade workflow follows.

categories.finding: Historic market difficulty → edge metaphor → portfolio chat → analysis → suggestion/confirmation → URL.
An exchange exterior and finance-related scenes identify the market theme before the tool is shown.
The portfolio reply at 21s makes the chat-finance function clear; the later request and confirm action establish trading.
Typed prompts, loading states, card appearance and button status changes are visible. Actual processing and order latency are not established.
The film moves sharply from adventure footage to white chat UI; repeated prompts and NVDA labels then connect the demo steps.
Historical-looking finance and blue-sky adventure footage contrast with a spare white interface.
Prompts and the confirmation button are enlarged, while market numbers and rationale are smaller and pass quickly.

categories.finding: The chat request/result and confirm/order-placed states communicate the workflow silently, though small setup details need more time.
Close views prioritize prompt writing and the green confirmation button; the rationale is subordinate in the card.
About 15s establish the market metaphor, then about 18s show two requests and an order sequence.
The difficult-market setup resolves into a simple conversational workflow; a genuine market advantage is not demonstrated.
Sports and parachute imagery may associate the tool with control and advantage; viewer response is unmeasured.
The specific NVDA request is carried into analysis, suggestion and confirmation, creating a coherent task chain.
The suggested position and order state are shown content, not verified advice or performance. Accuracy, risk treatment and execution were not independently checked.
Liquid branding and the explicit confirm step give the product a concrete identity within a familiar chat format.
Give the trade rationale and sizing a short readable pause before confirmation.
categories.experiment: Hold the suggestion card with three labeled fields: requested position, proposed size and reason, before the user confirms.

categories.finding: For Tin, preserve the visible confirmation step between an AI suggestion and an external action.
categories.experiment: Show an agent-proposed campaign change, a readable summary, user approval and the resulting published state.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Show analysis, a proposed action and a separate user confirmation in the same task chain.
try: Hold the proposal with readable position, size and reason before confirmation.
For Tin, show the proposed campaign change, approval summary and published result as separate visible steps.
lessons.avoid: Making the decision rationale harder to read than the action button.
lessons.open: Rationale clarity, model/tool behavior, market accuracy, execution and audio remain unverified.
